statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-21218 (GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw) is a .NET security feature bypass in System.Security.Cryptography.Cose: a crafted payload can bypass the library's security checks. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Cose 10.0.0 through 10.0.2 as affected and 10.0.3 as fixed, shipped with .NET 10.0.3 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/380, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.3/10.0.3.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries; 10.0.3-r0 is built from the v10.0.103 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.103). System.Security.Cryptography.Cose is not part of the .NET or ASP.NET Core shared frameworks; this owner ships it as the System.Security.Cryptography.Cose NuGet package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts. Checked the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: that package and its assemblies are version 10.0.2 in 10.0.2-r0 and 10.0.3 in 10.0.3-r0, and match the build's .NET version in every later build. The same version also appears as a reference assembly in the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.DotNetApiDocs.Transport package; no other System.Security.Cryptography.Cose assembly is in these packages (the dotnet-symbols-all archives hold only its .pdb debug symbols, and the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense package only its XML documentation). The range ends at 10.0.3-r0 because it is the first published build with the fixed package.

CVE-2026-21218 (GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw) is a .NET security feature bypass: a crafted payload can bypass security checks in System.Security.Cryptography.Cose. Microsoft lists the independently versioned System.Security.Cryptography.Cose package from 8.0.0 through 8.0.1 as affected and 8.0.2 as fixed, and the .NET 8.0.24 release ships System.Security.Cryptography.Cose 8.0.2 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/380, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.24/8.0.24.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. The only System.Security.Cryptography.Cose implementation code in them is the System.Security.Cryptography.Cose NuGet package held by dotnet8-runtime-artifacts: version 8.0.1, built from .NET 8.0.23, in 8.0.23-r0, and version 8.0.2, built from the build's own .NET release, in 8.0.24-r0 and every later build. dotnet8-runtime-artifacts also holds a System.Security.Cryptography.Cose reference assembly inside the .NET API documentation transport package, which carries no implementation code. The .NET 8 shared frameworks in these packages do not include System.Security.Cryptography.Cose.dll. The range ends at 8.0.24-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-21218 (GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw) is a .NET security feature bypass in System.Security.Cryptography.Cose: a crafted payload can bypass the library's security checks. Microsoft fixed the .NET 9 package in 9.0.13 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/380, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.13/9.0.13.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: System.Security.Cryptography.Cose.dll appears in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, inside the System.Security.Cryptography.Cose NuGet package (implementation and reference assembly), and in no other package; it is not part of the .NET or ASP.NET Core shared frameworks. In 9.0.12-r0 that package is 9.0.12, which is affected; from 9.0.13-r0 on, the version is 9.0.13 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
